newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Duma passes oil legislation in first reading.
newsitem.headline: Russian Duma passes oil legislation in first reading.

text.p: Russia's opposition-dominated State Duma, the lower parliament house, approved on Tuesday enabling legislation needed to make Russia's oil production-sharing law function.

Deputies approved the measure in a first reading with 231 votes for it and 120 against it. Three officials abstained from voting. The bill must pass two more Duma readings before going to the upper chamber, the Federation Council, for approval.

The enabling legislation, something foreign energy investors want to see, brings Russia's production-sharing law into line with other existing laws, thus helping open the door to an estimated $60 billion in planned foreign investment in Russia's energy sector.
U.S., Japanese, European and other oil companies are also waiting for Russia to approve a final list of oil reserves exploitable under production-sharing deals.

The original list numbered over 200 deposits but has been considerably winnowed over conservative deputies' fears that Russia will lose out if it opens its natural resources sector to outside investors.
